source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 257: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 257: do not choose tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the prompt alone. Assume the model graph/layer shapes, precision, parameter and activation sizes, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), topology and link bandwidth, software/runtime versions, clocks, request-length distribution, arrival rate, concurrency, batching policy, and explicit latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are known; label estimates separately from measured facts. Enumerate topology-aware TP degrees and balanced PP stage partitions, and reject any candidate without positive per-GPU memory headroom or a feasible reconfiguration plan. Falsifiable hypothesis: on identical hardware and a representative fixed workload, the feasible candidate with lower held-out p99 end-to-end latency while meeting every SLO gate is superior; falsify this if p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Warm up, randomize paired trials, tune only on disjoint data, then evaluate held-out requests while holding workload mix, arrival rate, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy constant. Measure per-GPU memory/headroom, compute time, TP collective or PP activation-transfer time, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline bubbles, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality, and recovery time with units and uncertainty. Stratify by request length and load; control software, thermal state, placement, retries, and interference; report sample counts and confidence intervals. Use only authorized isolated failure/reconfiguration tests. Require correctness, quality, memory, error-rate, availability, and latency gates, then canary the winner with monitoring and an abort threshold. Rollback to the last known-good configuration on any gate breach, failed health check, unsafe memory pressure, or regression; preserve evidence and document recovery.
risks: Missing platform facts and SLO thresholds prevent a universal TP/PP winner.
Tail latency is sensitive to batching, queueing, stage imbalance, collectives, stragglers, retries, and workload drift.
Unauthorized fault testing or canaries can disrupt service.
evidence_required: Per-GPU memory/headroom and topology measurements for feasible TP/PP configurations and partitions.
Repeated randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning and held-out p50/p95/p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, error, quality, and availability results.
Authorized isolated canary and recovery evidence, with gate thresholds, monitoring, and rollback records.
